You have high cortisol, chronic fatigue, poor sleep, brain fog, and sugar cravings are all signs that your cortisol is far too high. Let me tell you why this happens and what you can do about it. Cortisol is your body's stress hormone. It tells your body when to relax and when to panic, and when it stays high for too long, your body starts storing fat as if it were preparing for famine. Now here is what most people do not know. Cortisol does not just rise from work or from being busy. It rises from how you think, how you react, how you talk to yourself, from the emotions you accumulate without ever letting them go. Your stress mind keeps cortisol high, and high cortisol keeps your mind stressed. It is a cycle that feeds itself. That is why you feel anxious, exhausted, irritable, and cannot sleep. And that cycle does not break with dyes or pills. It breaks when you learn to calm what is happening inside of you. When your nervous system calms down, cortisol drops. When cortisol drops, your body stops holding onto fat, sleep returns, cravings disappear, and your mind finally clears. But nobody teaches you how to calm your nervous system. They tell you to exercise, eat better, meditate for five minutes, and all of that is fine, but it does not reach the root. The root is learning to let go, to stop reacting, to step out of the survival mode you have been living in every single day without even realizing it.
